chapters.title: The Great Day of the LORD Is Near
chapters.html:
Zephaniah 1

I Will Sweep Away Everything

1The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.

2I will utterly sweep away everything
from the face of the ground,
declares the LORD.

3I will sweep away man and beast;
I will sweep away the birds of the heavens
and the fish of the sea,
and the stumbling blocks with the wicked;
I will cut off humankind
from the face of the ground,
declares the LORD.

4I will stretch out My hand against Judah
and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem;
I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal,
the name of the idol priests with the priests,

5those who bow down on the rooftops
to the host of the heavens,
and those who bow down and swear to the LORD
and swear by Milcom,

6those who turn back from following the LORD,
who have not sought the LORD
or inquired of Him.

The Day of the LORD's Sacrifice

7Silence before the Lord GOD!
For the day of the LORD is near;
the LORD has prepared a sacrifice;
He has consecrated those He invited.

8And it shall come to pass on the day of the LORD's sacrifice
that I will punish the princes and the king's sons
and all who dress in foreign clothing.

9On that day I will punish
everyone who leaps over the threshold,
who fill their master's house
with violence and deceit.

10And it shall come to pass on that day, declares the LORD,
that there will be the sound of a cry from the Fish Gate,
a wail from the Second Quarter,
and a great crash from the hills.

11Wail, you who live in the Hollow,
for all the trading people are ruined;
all who weigh out silver are cut off.

12And it shall come to pass at that time
that I will search Jerusalem with lamps,
and punish the men who are settled on their dregs,
who say in their hearts,
"The LORD will not do good, nor will He do harm."

13Their wealth will become spoil,
and their houses a desolation;
they will build houses but not live in them,
and plant vineyards but not drink their wine.

A Day of Fury

14The great day of the LORD is near,
near and hurrying fast.
The sound of the day of the LORD!
The warrior cries out bitterly there.

15That day is a day of fury,
a day of distress and anguish,
a day of waste and desolation,
a day of darkness and gloom,
a day of cloud and thick darkness,

16a day of the horn and the battle cry
against the fortified cities
and against the high towers.

17I will bring distress on humankind,
and they will walk like the blind,
for they have sinned against the LORD;
their blood will be poured out like dust,
and their flesh like dung.

18Neither their silver nor their gold
will be able to rescue them
in the day of the LORD's fury;
in the fire of His jealousy
the whole earth will be consumed;
for He will make a full end, a sudden one,
of all the inhabitants of the earth.

Notes

  • v1 "Zephaniah son of Cushi… son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon" — the line goes back four generations, to a Hezekiah; the verse does not say whether he is King Hezekiah. Tsefanyah, Zephaniah, has the letters of tsafan, hide or treasure, with the LORD's name. Josiah began to reign as a boy, eight years old (2 Kings 22:1), and swept out the idol priests and the rooftop altars this chapter names (2 Kings 23:5, 12).

  • vv2–3 "I will utterly sweep away everything from the face of the ground… man and beast… the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea" — asof asef, word for word sweeping away I will sweep away. The list runs the creation backward, from man to the fish, and takes the flood's words, I will wipe away the human whom I created from upon the face of the ground — from human to beast, to creeping thing, and to the bird of the heavens (Genesis 6:7). Hosea uses the same verb of the land, even the fish of the sea are taken away (Hosea 4:3). Adam… adamah, humankind… the ground, sound alike. Ha-makhshelot et ha-resha'im, the stumbling blocks with the wicked, is obscure; mikhshol is the stumbling block of their iniquity, their idols (Ezekiel 14:3).

  • vv4–6 "the remnant of Baal, the name of the idol priests… swear to the LORD and swear by Milcom" — kemarim, idol priests, are those Josiah put down (2 Kings 23:5) and those of the calf (Hosea 10:5). The rooftop worship is Jeremiah's houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of heaven (Jeremiah 19:13). Malkam is read as Milcom, the god of the Ammonites, Milcom the loathsome thing of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11:5), as in Jeremiah 49:1; the same letters say their king, and the Greek has their king. They swear by the LORD and by Milcom at once.

  • vv7–8 "Silence before the Lord GOD!… the LORD has prepared a sacrifice; He has consecrated those He invited" — has, silence, as in Habakkuk 2:20. The feast is turned around: the guests are called to a sacrifice that is themselves. Hiqdish qeru'av, consecrated those He invited, as Samuel consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice (1 Samuel 16:5), and those who are invited eat after the blessing (1 Samuel 9:13). The LORD's sacrifice is a slaughter, as in the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah (Isaiah 34:6) and in the land of the north (Jeremiah 46:10).

  • v9 "everyone who leaps over the threshold… their master's house" — the priests of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon (1 Samuel 5:5); here those who leap over it are punished. Beit adoneihem, their master's house, may be a king's house, filled by servants with plunder, or a temple; the Greek has the house of the Lord their God.

  • vv10–11 "the Fish Gate… the Second Quarter… the Hollow… all the trading people" — places of Jerusalem: the Fish Gate (Nehemiah 3:3), and the Second Quarter, where the prophetess Huldah lived in Josiah's day (2 Kings 22:14). Ha-makhtesh, the Hollow, word for word the mortar, the word of the hollow place that is at Lehi (Judges 15:19). Am Kena'an is word for word the people of Canaan; Kena'an is also trader, as in A trader with false scales in his hand (Hosea 12:7), and the next line names them, all who weigh out silver.

  • vv12–13 "I will search Jerusalem with lamps… settled on their dregs… The LORD will not do good, nor will He do harm" — achappes, I will search, as Esau has been searched out (Obadiah 6). Qof'im al shimreihem, settled on their dregs, is wine left undisturbed, as Moab is settled on his dregs; he has not been poured from vessel to vessel (Jeremiah 48:11). Their creed is that the LORD does nothing, as the idols can do no harm, and neither is it in them to do good (Jeremiah 10:5). The curse is Amos's, you have built houses of dressed stone, but you will not live in them; you have planted pleasant vineyards, but you will not drink their wine (Amos 5:11).

  • vv14–16 "a day of fury… a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness… a day of the horn and the battle cry" — yom, day, seven times in vv15–16. Evrah, fury, as in Habakkuk 3:8. Tsarah u-metsuqah, distress and anguish, as in Distress and anguish terrify him (Job 15:24), and sho'ah u-mesho'ah, waste and desolation, two words of one sound, as in Job 30:3. A day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness is Joel 2:2 word for word, and the English is Joel's. Tsoreach, cries out, is found again only of the LORD Himself, He raises the battle cry (Isaiah 42:13). Teru'ah, battle cry, with the horn, as in Amos 2:2.

  • vv17–18 "they will walk like the blind… Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to rescue them in the day of the LORD's fury" — the curse of the law, You will grope at noon as the blind man gropes in darkness (Deuteronomy 28:29). Ke-gelalim, like dung, as in as one sweeps away dung (1 Kings 14:10). The silver and gold line is Ezekiel's, their silver and their gold will not be able to rescue them in the day of the LORD's fury (Ezekiel 7:19). The fire of His jealousy: the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God (Deuteronomy 4:24). Kol ha-arets, the whole earth, may also be the whole land; v2 spoke of the face of the ground.

chapters.title: Seek the LORD, All You Humble of the Land
chapters.html:
Zephaniah 2

Seek the LORD

1Gather yourselves together, yes, gather,
O nation without shame,

2before the decree gives birth —
the day passes like chaff —
before the burning anger of the LORD comes upon you,
before the day of the LORD's anger comes upon you.

3Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land,
who do His justice;
seek righteousness, seek humility;
perhaps you will be hidden
on the day of the LORD's anger.

Against the Philistines

4For Gaza will be forsaken,
and Ashkelon a desolation;
Ashdod will be driven out at noon,
and Ekron uprooted.

5Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast,
the nation of the Cherethites!
The word of the LORD is against you,
Canaan, land of the Philistines:
I will destroy you until no inhabitant is left.

6The seacoast will be pastures,
with meadows for shepherds
and folds for flocks.

7The coast will belong
to the remnant of the house of Judah;
they will graze on it;
in the houses of Ashkelon
they will lie down at evening;
for the LORD their God will visit them
and restore their fortunes.

Against Moab and Ammon

8I have heard the scorn of Moab
and the revilings of the sons of Ammon,
how they scorned My people
and boasted against their border.

9Therefore, as I live,
declares the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel,
Moab will become like Sodom,
and the sons of Ammon like Gomorrah,
a land possessed by nettles and salt pits,
a desolation forever;
the remnant of My people will plunder them,
and the rest of My nation will inherit them.

10This they will have for their pride,
because they scorned and boasted
against the people of the LORD of hosts.

11The LORD will be fearsome against them,
for He will starve all the gods of the earth;
and they will bow down to Him, each from his place,
all the coastlands of the nations.

Against Cush and Assyria

12You too, Cushites —
they are slain by My sword.

13He will stretch out His hand against the north
and destroy Assyria,
and He will make Nineveh a desolation,
dry as the wilderness.

14Herds will lie down inside her,
every kind of beast;
the pelican and the hedgehog
will lodge in her capitals;
a voice will sing in the window;
desolation will be on the threshold;
for the cedar work is laid bare.

15This is the exultant city
that sat secure,
that said in her heart,
"I am, and there is none besides me."
How she has become a desolation,
a lair for wild beasts!
Everyone who passes by her
will hiss and shake his hand.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Gather yourselves together, yes, gather, O nation without shame… the day passes like chaff" — hitqoshshu va-qoshu, gather yourselves… gather, is the verb of gathering stubble, qash: the nation is told to gather as straw is gathered. Lo nikhsaf, without shame, from kasaf, which is long for, as in you deeply longed for your father's house (Genesis 31:30): the nation may be one not longed for, or one that does not grow pale with shame. The Greek has the undisciplined nation. v2 is partly obscure: be-terem ledet choq, before the decree gives birth. The chaff is Hosea's, like chaff that is whirled from the threshing floor (Hosea 13:3).

  • v3 "Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land… perhaps you will be hidden" — anvei ha-arets, the humble of the land, as in decide with fairness for the humble of the earth (Isaiah 11:4), the humble whom the rich turn aside in Amos 2:7. Bakkeshu, seek, three times. Ulai, perhaps, is Amos's word, perhaps the LORD, the God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph (Amos 5:15): nothing is promised, only the hope.

  • vv4–5 "Gaza will be forsaken… Ekron uprooted… the nation of the Cherethites" — the four Philistine cities of Amos 1:6–8, each with a play on its name: Azzah azuvah, Gaza… forsaken, and Eqron te'aqer, Ekron… uprooted. Kerethim, Cherethites, named here with the Philistines, as in the Negev of the Cherethites (1 Samuel 30:14), sounds like karat, cut off, as in Ezekiel's I will cut off the Cherethites (Ezekiel 25:16). Chevel ha-yam, the seacoast, word for word the cord of the sea, a measured stretch of land, the measuring line of Micah 2:5. Kena'an, Canaan, names Philistia here.

  • vv6–7 "pastures, with meadows for shepherds… for the LORD their God will visit them and restore their fortunes" — kerot, meadows, is uncertain, and sounds like Kerethim (v5); the Greek has Crete. Yifqedem, will visit them, is the verb of 1:8–9, I will punish: the LORD's coming is punishment for some and care for others, as in Joseph's God will surely visit you (Genesis 50:24). Shav shevitam, restore their fortunes, as in Joel 3:1.

  • vv8–10 "the scorn of Moab and the revilings of the sons of Ammon… like Sodom… like Gomorrah… for their pride" — Moab and Ammon were born from Lot's daughters after Sodom (Genesis 19:37–38), and their end is Sodom's, as the law foretold of a cursed land, sulfur and salt… like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Deuteronomy 29:23). Giddufei, revilings, is the verb of the Assyrian servants who reviled Me (2 Kings 19:6). Ge'onam, their pride, as in Jeremiah's We have heard of the pride of Moab (Jeremiah 48:29). Mimshaq, a land possessed by, and mikhreh melach, salt pits, are found only here. Written goy, read goyi, My nation.

  • v11 "He will starve all the gods of the earth… all the coastlands of the nations" — razah, starve, make lean, as in the fat of his flesh will grow lean (Isaiah 17:4). Iyyei ha-goyim, the coastlands of the nations, the phrase of the table of nations (Genesis 10:5). Each from his place: the nations bow down where they are.

  • vv12–13 "You too, Cushites… He will make Nineveh a desolation" — the oracles have gone from Philistia to Moab and Ammon, and now to Cush and to Assyria, against the north. The Cushites are spoken to, then spoken of, in one line. Nineveh's fall, told in Nahum, is here foretold in a few words, dry as the wilderness.

  • vv14–15 "the pelican and the hedgehog… I am, and there is none besides me… Everyone who passes by her will hiss" — qa'at ve-qippod, the pelican and the hedgehog, are the creatures of ruined Edom in Isaiah, The pelican and the hedgehog will possess it (Isaiah 34:11). Kaftoreha, her capitals, the tops of pillars, as in Strike the capitals (Amos 9:1). The rest of v14 is obscure: chorev ba-saf, desolation on the threshold, where the Greek has ravens, orev, nearly the same letters; arzah, cedar work, is found only here. Nineveh's boast is Babylon's in Isaiah, who sits secure, who says in her heart, "I am, and there is none besides me" (Isaiah 47:8). Ha-alizah, exultant, as in an exultant town (Isaiah 22:2). The hissing is that of ruins, everyone who passes by it will be horrified and will hiss (Jeremiah 49:17).

chapters.title: He Will Rejoice over You with Singing
chapters.html:
Zephaniah 3

Woe to the Oppressing City

1Woe to her who rebels and is defiled,
the oppressing city!

2She has not listened to the voice;
she has not taken correction;
she has not trusted in the LORD;
she has not drawn near to her God.

3Her princes within her are roaring lions;
her judges are wolves of the evening
that leave nothing for the morning.

4Her prophets are reckless,
men of treachery;
her priests have profaned what is holy;
they have done violence to the law.

5The LORD within her is righteous;
He does no injustice.
Morning by morning He brings His justice to light;
He does not fail.
But the unjust knows no shame.

6I have cut off nations;
their towers are desolate;
I have laid waste their streets,
with no one passing through;
their cities are devastated,
with no man, no inhabitant.

7I said, "Surely you will fear Me;
you will take correction";
then her dwelling would not be cut off
for all that I had appointed against her.
But they rose early to ruin all their deeds.

8Therefore wait for Me, declares the LORD,
for the day I rise up to the prey;
for My decision is to gather nations,
to assemble kingdoms,
to pour out on them My indignation,
all My burning anger;
for in the fire of My jealousy
the whole earth will be consumed.

A Pure Lip

9For then I will change the peoples to a pure lip,
so that all of them may call on the name of the LORD
and serve Him shoulder to shoulder.

10From beyond the rivers of Cush
those who plead with Me, the daughter of My scattered ones,
will bring My offering.

11On that day you will not be put to shame
for all your deeds by which you rebelled against Me;
for then I will remove from within you
those who exult in your pride,
and you will no longer be haughty
on My holy mountain.

12I will leave within you
a people humble and poor,
and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.

13The remnant of Israel will do no injustice
and speak no lies,
and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths;
for they will graze and lie down,
with no one to make them afraid.

Sing, Daughter of Zion

14Sing aloud, daughter of Zion;
shout, Israel!
Rejoice and exult with all your heart,
daughter of Jerusalem!

15The LORD has taken away the judgments against you;
He has turned away your enemy.
The King of Israel, the LORD, is within you;
you will never again fear evil.

16On that day it will be said to Jerusalem:
"Do not fear, Zion;
let not your hands go limp.

17The LORD your God is within you,
a warrior who saves;
He will rejoice over you with gladness;
He will be silent in His love;
He will exult over you with singing."

18Those who grieve, away from the appointed feast, I will gather;
they were from you,
a burden on her, a reproach.

19I am about to deal with all who afflict you
at that time;
I will save the lame
and gather the outcast,
and I will make them a praise and a name
in all the earth where they were put to shame.

20At that time I will bring you in,
at the time when I gather you;
for I will make you a name and a praise
among all the peoples of the earth,
when I restore your fortunes before your eyes,
says the LORD.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Woe to her who rebels and is defiled, the oppressing city!… she has not taken correction" — the city is not named until v14: after the woes on the nations (chapter 2), Jerusalem is next. Nig'alah, defiled, as in your hands are defiled with blood (Isaiah 59:3). Ha-ir ha-yonah, the oppressing city, as in the oppressing sword (Jeremiah 46:16); yonah is also dove, the name of Jonah, and the Greek has the dove. Lo laqechah musar, she has not taken correction, are Jeremiah's words, This is the nation that did not obey the voice of the LORD its God and did not take correction (Jeremiah 7:28). In Swete's Greek this chapter begins one verse earlier, with 2:15.

  • vv3–4 "Her princes within her are roaring lions… her priests have profaned what is holy; they have done violence to the law" — the same four, princes, judges, prophets and priests, stand in Ezekiel's charge against Jerusalem: Her priests have done violence to My law and profaned My holy things (Ezekiel 22:26), Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing prey (Ezekiel 22:27). Wolves of the evening as in Habakkuk 1:8. Lo garmu la-boqer, leave nothing for the morning, word for word gnaw no bone for the morning: garam is the verb of crush their bones (Numbers 24:8). Pochazim, reckless, as in worthless and reckless men (Judges 9:4).

  • v5 "The LORD within her is righteous… Morning by morning He brings His justice to light… But the unjust knows no shame" — be-qirbah, within her, the same word as her princes within her (v3): the LORD and the princes are in one city, and only one of them does justice. Lo ya'aseh avlah, He does no injustice, as in A God of faithfulness and without wrong (Deuteronomy 32:4), and the remnant will be the same (v13). Lo ne'dar, He does not fail, as in not one is missing (Isaiah 40:26). The unjust, like Jeremiah's people, did not know how to blush (Jeremiah 6:15).

  • vv6–8 "they rose early to ruin all their deeds… for the day I rise up to the prey" — hishkimu hishchitu, they rose early to ruin: what they were eager for was ruin, as when all flesh had ruined its way upon the earth (Genesis 6:12). Le-ad, to the prey, as pointed, the word of Benjamin's blessing, In the morning he eats the prey (Genesis 49:27); the same letters read le-ed, as a witness, and the Greek has for a witness, as in let the Lord GOD be a witness against you (Micah 1:2). In the fire of My jealousy the whole earth will be consumed is 1:18 again, now in the LORD's own mouth.

  • vv9–10 "I will change the peoples to a pure lip… From beyond the rivers of Cush" — safah, lip, is the word of Babel, All the earth was one lip… let us confuse their lip there (Genesis 11:1, 7): the confusion is undone, and the one lip is pure. Ehpokh, I will change, is hafakh, the overturning of Jonah 3:4. Shekhem echad, word for word one shoulder, shoulder to shoulder. Me-ever le-naharei Khush, from beyond the rivers of Cush, is Isaiah's phrase (Isaiah 18:1), where a gift will be brought to the LORD of hosts (Isaiah 18:7). Atarai, those who plead with Me, is the verb of Isaac, who pleaded with the LORD (Genesis 25:21).

  • vv11–13 "those who exult in your pride… a people humble and poor… with no one to make them afraid" — alizei ga'avatekh, those who exult in your pride, are Isaiah's words for the LORD's own warriors, those who exult in My majesty (Isaiah 13:3), turned on Jerusalem's proud; alizah, exultant, was Nineveh's word (2:15). Le-govhah, be haughty, as in Do not keep talking so very proudly (1 Samuel 2:3). The remnant is the humble of 2:3, who take refuge in the LORD as in Nahum 1:7. Leshon tarmit, a deceitful tongue, as in the deceit of their own hearts (Jeremiah 14:14). Ve-ein macharid, with no one to make them afraid, is Micah 4:4.

  • vv14–15 "Sing aloud, daughter of Zion… The King of Israel, the LORD, is within you" — ronni, sing aloud, as in Sing, barren one (Isaiah 54:1); hari'u, shout, is the verb of the alarm in Joel 2:1, now a shout of joy. The judgments taken away are the sentences of chapters 1 and 3. The LORD… within you answers the false boast, Is not the LORD among us? (Micah 3:11), and the LORD within her who saw her injustice (v5). You will never again fear evil, as in I fear no evil, for You are with me (Psalm 23:4).

  • vv16–17 "let not your hands go limp… a warrior who saves… He will be silent in His love" — al yirpu yadayikh, let not your hands go limp, as Ishbosheth's hands went limp at Abner's death (2 Samuel 4:1). Gibbor yoshia, a warrior who saves: the warrior who cried out bitterly on the day of the LORD (1:14) is answered by the LORD as warrior. Yasis alayikh, He will rejoice over you, as in so your God will rejoice over you (Isaiah 62:5). Yacharish be-ahavato, He will be silent in His love, is the verb of Habakkuk's keep silent (Habakkuk 1:13), now love's stillness; the Greek has He will renew you in His love, yechaddesh, nearly the same letters.

  • vv18–20 "Those who grieve, away from the appointed feast… I will save the lame and gather the outcast… a name and a praise" — v18 is obscure; its words are those of Lamentations, no one comes to the appointed feasts… her virgins are grieving (Lamentations 1:4). v19 is Micah's promise, I will gather the lame and assemble the outcast (Micah 4:6). A praise and a name is the law's, for praise and for a name and for glory (Deuteronomy 26:19). Restore your fortunes as in 2:7. The book that opened with the LORD sweeping away everything (1:2) ends with Him gathering.

speech.text: Zephaniah 3
Woe to the Oppressing City
Woe to her who rebels and is defiled, the oppressing city!
She has not listened to the voice; she has not taken correction; she has not trusted in the LORD; she has not drawn near to her God.
Her princes within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves of the evening that leave nothing for the morning.
Her prophets are reckless, men of treachery; her priests have profaned what is holy; they have done violence to the law.
The LORD within her is righteous; He does no injustice. Morning by morning He brings His justice to light; He does not fail. But the unjust knows no shame.
I have cut off nations; their towers are desolate; I have laid waste their streets, with no one passing through; their cities are devastated, with no man, no inhabitant.
I said, "Surely you will fear Me; you will take correction"; then her dwelling would not be cut off for all that I had appointed against her. But they rose early to ruin all their deeds.

Therefore wait for Me, declares the LORD, for the day I rise up to the prey; for My decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out on them My indignation, all My burning anger; for in the fire of My jealousy the whole earth will be consumed.
A Pure Lip
For then I will change the peoples to a pure lip, so that all of them may call on the name of the LORD and serve Him shoulder to shoulder.
From beyond the rivers of Cush those who plead with Me, the daughter of My scattered ones, will bring My offering.

On that day you will not be put to shame for all your deeds by which you rebelled against Me; for then I will remove from within you those who exult in your pride, and you will no longer be haughty on My holy mountain.
I will leave within you a people humble and poor, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
The remnant of Israel will do no injustice and speak no lies, and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths; for they will graze and lie down, with no one to make them afraid.
Sing, Daughter of Zion
Sing aloud, daughter of Zion; shout, Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem!
The LORD has taken away the judgments against you; He has turned away your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is within you; you will never again fear evil.
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: "Do not fear, Zion; let not your hands go limp.
The LORD your God is within you, a warrior who saves; He will rejoice over you with gladness; He will be silent in His love; He will exult over you with singing."
Those who grieve, away from the appointed feast, I will gather; they were from you, a burden on her, a reproach.
I am about to deal with all who afflict you at that time; I will save the lame and gather the outcast, and I will make them a praise and a name in all the earth where they were put to shame.

At that time I will bring you in, at the time when I gather you; for I will make you a name and a praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says the LORD.
